extraction.name: LAMBADA
extraction.description: LAMBADA is a dataset for evaluating computational models of text understanding through a word prediction task. It consists of narrative passages from the Book Corpus where human subjects can guess the last word of the target sentence when given the whole passage, but not when given only the target sentence. The dataset contains 10,022 passages divided into development and test sets.
extraction.creator: Denis Paperno; Germán Kruszewski; Angeliki Lazaridou; Quan Ngoc Pham; Raffaella Bernardi; Sandro Pezzelle; Marco Baroni; Gemma Boleda; Raquel Fernández
extraction.citeAs: Denis Paperno, Germán Kruszewski, Angeliki Lazaridou, Quan Ngoc Pham, Raffaella Bernardi, Sandro Pezzelle, Marco Baroni, Gemma Boleda, and Raquel Fernández. 2016. The LAMBADA dataset: Word prediction requiring a broad discourse context.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was built from passages drawn from the Book Corpus of unpublished novels. The authors randomly divided the novels into training and development+testing partitions, constructed LAMBADA from the development+testing partition, filtered out passages that standard language models found relatively easy, and then retained only passages that passed a three-step human evaluation pipeline on CrowdFlower.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis; Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The source data were passages from the Book Corpus, which after duplicate removal and filtering of potentially offensive material contained 5,325 unpublished novels and 465 million words.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: A random sample of passages was evaluated by human subjects through the CrowdFlower crowdsourcing service in three steps: one subject guessed the target word from the whole passage; if correct, a second subject guessed from the whole passage; if also correct, additional subjects guessed from the target sentence only until the word was guessed or 10 unsuccessful guesses were reached, and passages were kept only if two whole-passage subjects exactly matched the missing word and no sentence-only subject could guess it; subjects in step 3 were allowed 3 guesses per sentence, and the same subject could not judge the same item in both passage and sentence conditions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Passages were added to the dataset only if two consecutive subjects exactly matched the missing word using the whole passage and no subject out of ten could provide it from the target sentence alone, even with 3 guesses.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: a pre-trained recurrent neural network (RNN); a standard 4-gram model; a RNN; a feed-forward model
extraction.rai:dataBiases: proper nouns are hugely overrepresented in LAMBADA, while the other categories are under-represented, compared to the POS distribution in the input; LAMBADA items contain (quoted) direct speech significantly more often than the input items overall (71% of LAMBADA items vs. 61% of items in the input sample)
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: the evaluation we performed is very preliminary, and it must only be taken as a proof-of-concept study of the difficulty of LAMBADA; standard language models are bound to fail on it by design: one of our first filters was to choose passages where a number of simple language models were failing to predict the upcoming word; cost considerations precluded us from using more subjects at stage 1, which could in principle improve the quality of filtering at this step
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: the corpus, after duplicate removal and filtering out of potentially offensive material with a stop word list, contains 5,325 novels and 465 million words
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: a dataset to evaluate the capabilities of computational models for text understanding by means of a word prediction task; a challenging test set meant to encourage the development of new models capable of genuine understanding of broad context in natural language text; a tool to evaluate general-purpose models in terms of how they fare on broad-context understanding
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: the development set of LAMBADA, along with the training corpus, can be downloaded; the test set will be made available at the time of the competition
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The corpus, after duplicate removal and filtering out of potentially offensive material with a stop word list, contains 5,325 novels and 465 million words. We randomly divided the novels into equally-sized training and development+testing partitions. To reduce time and cost of dataset collection, we filtered out passages that are relatively easy for standard language models. Any passage whose target word had probability ≥0.00175 according to any of the language models was excluded.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The corpus, after duplicate removal and filtering out of potentially offensive material with a stop word list, contains 5,325 novels and 465 million words.
